items.stem:
Relative protease activity versus pH for two digestive enzymes:

pH | pepsin | trypsin
1.5 | 90 | 0
2.0 | 100 | 0
4.0 | 40 | 2
6.0 | 5 | 20
8.0 | 0 | 100
9.0 | 0 | 70

Stomach chyme is pH 2; pancreatic juice raises duodenal pH to 8. Which division of labour is consistent with the table?

choices.text: Pepsin accounts for gastric protein hydrolysis; trypsin is inactive there and becomes the principal duodenal endopeptidase after bicarbonate arrives
Trypsin is the stomach enzyme because digestion always begins with the enzyme that peaks at pH 8
Both enzymes work equally at pH 6, so the stomach and duodenum are interchangeable
Pepsin is a duodenal enzyme that is secreted in inactive form at pH 8

items.explanation: Pepsin’s activity is essentially 100 at gastric pH 2 and 0 at duodenal pH 8, so it cannot continue after bicarbonate arrives. Trypsin is 0 at pH 2 and 100 at pH 8, so it is silent in the stomach and dominant in the duodenum. The enzymes therefore act in series along the pH gradient, not as a single pH-6 compromise (where both are weak). Assigning trypsin to the stomach or pepsin to the duodenum contradicts the pH–activity columns.

distractorRationales.B: Trypsin has zero activity at pH 1.5–2, so it cannot be the gastric protease.
distractorRationales.C: At pH 6 pepsin is 5 and trypsin is 20, both far below their maxima, and neither organ is held at pH 6 in the stem.
distractorRationales.D: Pepsin is already at its maximum in the pH 2 column, the stomach condition, not at pH 8.

passage.title: Official Adjectives (1982)
passage.body: Kwame Boateng published “Official Adjectives” in 1982 after a season in municipal archives. The argument is that the archive is a construction site, not a warehouse. A paragraph concedes that not every complaint is evidence of capture. The turn is that the complaint is not against method but against unacknowledged method. Examples accumulate without becoming a catalogue — a mistranslated notice, a map that omits a creek, a hiring rubric that scores “fit.” The prose is dry rather than outraged; the heat is in what is treated as obvious. A late paragraph asks what would have to be true for the current procedure to be called fair, and then shows that those conditions are not met. The essay does not offer a slogan. It offers a test: if a practice cannot survive being described without its official adjectives, the adjectives were doing the work. Readers who want a policy list will be disappointed; readers who want to see how a tone becomes a rule will not.

items.stem: Suppose a planning authority publishes the unedited comment record beside its decision and states: “We heard the objections and are proceeding anyway, for the following reasons.” How would this information affect the author's argument?

choices.text: It would refute the argument, because any remaining objection after a statement of reasons proves that consultation never occurred.
It would be irrelevant, because the author cares only about whether sticky notes were used in the room.
It would weaken the argument by showing that photographs of halls are after all the essence of democracy.
It would instantiate the more honest practice the author recommends, shifting legitimacy from a listening-face to an attributable choice, without requiring that objectors prevail.

items.explanation: The sixth paragraph describes exactly this practice: do not abandon rooms; stop narrating them as consent machines; publish the unedited record; say we heard you and are proceeding anyway, for these reasons. New information that a city does that would count as the recommended alternative, not as a refutation. Objectors need not win for the conversion problem to be addressed; the issue was borrowed moral credit and the disappearance of choice. The photograph is what this statement is meant to replace. Incorporating the hypothetical therefore confirms D rather than a claim that reasons make consultation impossible.

distractorRationales.A: The author never equates objectors losing with the nonexistence of consultation; the expensive sentence is honest precisely when the project still proceeds.
distractorRationales.B: Sticky notes are opening scenery, not the criterion of legitimacy; unedited records and attributable reasons are the stated alternative.
distractorRationales.C: The photograph is criticized as allowing a government to be seen listening without being seen choosing; a reasons statement is the opposite of that preference.

passage.title: Minutes as consent
passage.body:
City governments have learned to speak the language of invitation. A new waterfront, a bus garage, a night-time licensing scheme: each arrives with a room, a facilitator, sticky notes, and a promise that "your voice will be heard." The promise is not empty in the way cynics assume. People do speak. Minutes are taken. A summary slide later reports that the community was "engaged." What the ritual converts, with almost chemical reliability, is dissent into attendance. The fact of having been in the room is then cited as evidence that the decision which followed was shared.

This conversion is the point, not an accidental side-effect. A planning authority that can display a photograph of a crowded hall has already performed legitimacy. The photograph does not record what was refused, only that refusal was given a chair. Once refusal has a chair, it can be filed. The file then travels upward as proof of consultation, and the project proceeds under the borrowed moral credit of those who came to object. Objectors discover, sometimes only at the groundbreaking, that they were extras in a scene titled participation.

The objection is not that consultation is a trick in every case. Some rooms change designs. A ramp is added; a tree is spared; a night bus is rerouted. Those revisions matter, and it would be a different piety to pretend they never occur. The trouble is the ambient theory that treats any revision as proof that the process is sound, and any remaining grievance as leftover noise from people who "had their chance." Attendance is thereby made to do the work of consent. Consent, if the word still means anything civic, is not the same as having been scheduled.

Oral comments at a microphone illustrate the substitution with painful clarity. Three minutes are allotted. A timer is visible. The speaker is thanked. The next speaker is invited. The form is courteous and the structure is a funnel: complexity is shaved to fit the slot, and what cannot be shaved is classified as repetition. Staff later write that "themes" emerged. Themes are what survive the funnel. They are not necessarily what the speakers thought they had said. A person who came to argue that the garage should not be built at all finds herself listed under "requests for mitigation." The minutes have translated abolition into upholstery.

Digital portals repeat the same conversion with a friendlier interface. A comment box invites "feedback." Character limits and dropdown menus decide in advance which kinds of sentence will count as input. The resident who types a structural objection is asked, before submitting, to rate the project from one to five stars. The rating is the datum that will be averaged; the paragraph is optional texture. When officials later announce that the "average rating was 3.7," they are not lying about the arithmetic. They are treating a coerced metric as a public will.

A more honest practice would not abandon rooms or portals. It would stop narrating them as consent machines. It would publish the unedited record beside the decision, including the proposals that were not adopted, and it would say plainly: we heard you and we are proceeding anyway, for these reasons. That sentence is politically expensive, which is why the photograph of the hall is preferred. The photograph allows a government to be seen listening without being seen choosing. Democracy, however, is not a listening face. It is the willingness to let a choice remain attributable, especially when the choice disappoints the people who were invited to speak.

items.stem: Based on the results, what is the most likely role of ReguFactor B in regulating HSP-70X expression during heat stress?

items.explanation: Overexpressing ReguFactor B increases HSP-70X mRNA (more activator → more activation), while knocking it out almost eliminates HSP-70X mRNA even under heat stress (no activator → no activation). Both results point the same direction: ReguFactor B switches HSP-70X ON. Overexpression and knockout results are two ends of the same lever — if more of a regulator means more of the target gene's expression, and less of the regulator means less expression, the regulator is an activator. If the pattern were reversed, it would be a repressor. Memory tip: "Push up, push down": if pushing the regulator up pushes the target up, and pushing it down pushes the target down, they're moving together — that's an activator, not a repressor (which would move the target the opposite way). Source: gamsat-trainer original practice (not ACER). Unverified.

passage.title: Biology · Gene Regulation
passage.body: A research group is studying a heat-shock protein gene, HSP-70X, thought to help wheat seedlings survive short bursts of extreme heat. They suspect a regulatory protein, called ReguFactor B, switches HSP-70X on when temperatures rise. To test this, they create three groups of genetically modified wheat seedlings: one where ReguFactor B is overexpressed (produced in excess), one where the gene for ReguFactor B is knocked out (disabled), and a normal (wild-type) control group. All seedlings are exposed to a two-hour heat spike, and HSP-70X mRNA levels are measured immediately afterwards. The overexpression group shows HSP-70X mRNA levels roughly four times higher than the wild-type control. The knockout group shows almost no detectable HSP-70X mRNA at all, even after the heat spike. Under normal, non-heat conditions, HSP-70X mRNA levels are low and roughly equal across all three groups.

items.stem: At the neuromuscular junction, acetylcholine opens a pentameric ligand-gated cation channel. Alpha-bungarotoxin occupies the acetylcholine-binding site without opening the channel. The toxin therefore:

choices.text: Increases end-plate potentials by blocking acetylcholinesterase
Converts the nicotinic receptor into a Gs-coupled GPCR that raises cAMP
Prevents end-plate depolarization by competitively blocking the ionotropic nicotinic ACh receptor
Blocks axonal voltage-gated sodium channels as its only high-affinity target at the end plate

items.explanation: The muscle nicotinic acetylcholine receptor is a ligand-gated ion channel (ionotropic): ACh binding opens a cation pore and depolarizes the end plate toward threshold. Alpha-bungarotoxin is a competitive antagonist at that site, so the channel stays closed, EPPs fall, and paralysis follows. It is not an acetylcholinesterase inhibitor (those raise ACh and can increase EPPs). Muscarinic receptors are GPCRs; the NMJ end-plate receptor is nicotinic and ionotropic. Voltage-gated Na+ channels in the surrounding sarcolemma fire after the EPP; bungarotoxin's defining NMJ action is on nAChR, not Nav.

distractorRationales.A: Cholinesterase inhibitors increase ACh; bungarotoxin occupies the receptor and shrinks EPPs.
distractorRationales.B: Nicotinic NMJ receptors are ion channels, not Gs-coupled muscarinic receptors.
distractorRationales.D: The toxin’s classic neuromuscular target is nAChR, not axonal Nav.

passage.title: The borrowed coat
passage.body:
He wore other people's sentences the way some men wear coats: against weather, and with the labels left in. At the seminar he began, "One might argue," and then produced, almost unaltered, a paragraph his supervisor had emailed at midnight to save him. The room nodded. He felt the coat settle on his shoulders, warm and slightly too large in the sleeves.

Afterward a friend said, "That was the first time you sounded like yourself." He laughed too quickly. In the bathroom mirror the coat was still on. He tried to take it off by telling the truth to the glass: I do not know whether I think this. The glass, being a glass, offered his mouth moving.

Ethics talks as if authenticity were a mineral you either contain or fake. The evening suggested something cheaper and more ordinary. A borrowed argument can keep you from freezing. It can also teach your arms the wrong length. The crime, if there is one, is not the borrowing. It is the nod you collect as if the sleeves had always been yours.

He sent the supervisor a note: Thank you. I sounded like myself. He deleted it. He sent: Thank you. I used your paragraph. He left that one in the outbox until morning, which is a kind of cowardice that still knows the difference.

items.stem:
Enthalpies of hydrogenation (kJ mol−1, all exothermic):

Compound | ΔHhyd
Cyclohexene | −120
Cyclohexa-1,3-diene | −230
Benzene | −210
Hypothetical ‘cyclohexatriene’ (3 × cyclohexene) | −360

Aromatic stabilisation is the gap between the hypothetical triene and real benzene. What is that energy, and which comparison shows conjugation in the diene is small?

choices.text: 150 kJ mol−1 aromatic stabilisation of benzene; the diene is only 10 kJ mol−1 more stable than two isolated double bonds (2 × −120 = −240 versus −230)
210 kJ mol−1, equal to benzene’s ΔHhyd, is the resonance energy
Benzene is 150 kJ mol−1 less stable than cyclohexatriene, because −210 is less negative than −360
The diene’s −230 versus benzene’s −210 shows the diene is more aromatic

items.explanation: Three isolated double bonds would release 360 kJ mol−1 on hydrogenation. Benzene releases only 210, so it starts 150 kJ mol−1 lower in energy: the aromatic stabilisation. Cyclohexa-1,3-diene at −230 versus −240 for two isolated alkenes is a mere 10 kJ mol−1 conjugation effect, not aromaticity. Resonance energy is that 150 kJ mol−1 gap, not the raw −210. Less negative ΔHhyd means the reactant was already lower in energy, i.e. more stable, not less. Aromaticity is the large benzene gap, not the slightly less exothermic hydrogenation of benzene versus the diene taken in isolation.

distractorRationales.B: −210 kJ mol−1 is the observed hydrogenation enthalpy, not the extra stabilisation relative to a Kekulé triene.
distractorRationales.C: A less exothermic hydrogenation means benzene is more stable than the hypothetical triene by 150 kJ mol−1.
distractorRationales.D: The 150 kJ mol−1 benzene gap dwarfs the diene’s 10 kJ mol−1; benzene is the aromatic partner.

passage.title: Unacknowledged Method (1978)
passage.body: In “Unacknowledged Method” (1978), Yuki Tanaka writes from inside urban cycling. The argument is that the archive is a construction site, not a warehouse. The author grants that standards exist for a reason and that amateurs can be wrong. The turn is that the complaint is not against method but against unacknowledged method. Examples accumulate without becoming a catalogue — a mistranslated notice, a map that omits a creek, a hiring rubric that scores “fit.” The prose is dry rather than outraged; the heat is in what is treated as obvious. A late paragraph asks what would have to be true for the current procedure to be called fair, and then shows that those conditions are not met. The essay does not offer a slogan. It offers a test: if a practice cannot survive being described without its official adjectives, the adjectives were doing the work. Readers who want a policy list will be disappointed; readers who want to see how a tone becomes a rule will not.

items.stem: Acetic acid (bp 118 °C) boils substantially higher than ethanol (bp 78 °C) even though their molar masses are similar (60 vs 46 g/mol). In nonpolar solvents, acetic acid is known to form cyclic dimers. Which description best links that dimerization to the elevated boiling point of neat acetic acid?

choices.text: Each dimer is held by two O–H···O hydrogen bonds, so more energy is required to produce separated gas-phase monomers than for ethanol’s single-donor hydrogen bonding.
Acetic acid dimers are covalently fused into a new compound with twice the molecular weight, and covalent dimers cannot evaporate.
Ethanol cannot hydrogen-bond at all, so any carboxylic acid will boil higher for reasons unrelated to dimers.
The dimers are ionic pairs of acetate and hydronium, producing salt-like boiling points.

items.explanation: Carboxylic acids in the liquid and in the vapor near the boiling point are strongly associated as cyclic dimers, each pair sharing two hydrogen bonds. Breaking that association to reach a gas of monomers (or of still-associated but fewer contacts) costs more enthalpy than disrupting ethanol’s singly donated hydrogen bonds. The dimers are still molecular hydrogen-bonded pairs, not new covalent molecules and not acetate–hydronium salts. Ethanol does hydrogen-bond, which is why it already boils well above propane; acetic acid’s extra donor–acceptor pair in the dimer pushes the boiling point higher still.

distractorRationales.B: Dimerization is a reversible hydrogen-bonding equilibrium, not formation of a new covalently bonded C–C or C–O framework that cannot vaporize.
distractorRationales.C: Ethanol is a classic hydrogen-bonding liquid; the comparison is dimer versus single H-bond, not H-bond versus none.
distractorRationales.D: Neat acetic acid is a molecular liquid of largely undissociated dimers, not an ionic melt of hydronium acetate.

items.stem:
The gas-phase reaction N2(g) + O2(g) ⇌ 2 NO(g) is studied in a sealed vessel. Equilibrium constants measured at three temperatures are:

T (K) | Kc
1500 | 1.0 × 10^−5
2000 | 4.0 × 10^−4
2500 | 3.5 × 10^−3

Kc = [NO]^2 / ([N2][O2]). Which conclusion is supported by the table?

choices.text: The forward reaction is exothermic, because Kc is small at 1500 K.
Kc increases with T only because the rate of the forward reaction increases; the equilibrium composition is unaffected by T.
The mixture is always reactant-favoured at every temperature listed, so heating cannot increase the equilibrium amount of NO.
The forward reaction is endothermic: raising T increases Kc, so the equilibrium yield of NO increases.

items.explanation: Van’t Hoff behaviour for an endothermic forward reaction is that K increases with temperature. The table shows Kc rising by more than two orders of magnitude from 1500 K to 2500 K, so the forward direction absorbs heat. A larger Kc means a larger equilibrium [NO]^2 / ([N2][O2]), hence a higher equilibrium yield of NO at the higher temperature (at comparable total pressure). A small Kc at 1500 K does not by itself prove the reaction is exothermic; the temperature trend of Kc is the thermodynamic signal. Rates affect how fast equilibrium is reached, not the value of Kc.

distractorRationales.A: A small Kc at one temperature does not establish that the forward reaction is exothermic. The increase of Kc with T is the signature of an endothermic forward reaction.
distractorRationales.B: Temperature changes both rates, but Kc is the ratio of rate constants (or a ΔG° function) and does change with T; the equilibrium composition therefore changes.
distractorRationales.C: Even when Kc remains less than 1, a larger Kc still corresponds to a larger equilibrium mole fraction of NO. Heating therefore does increase the equilibrium yield.

items.stem: Primary dermal fibroblasts are cultured in ascorbate-free medium and pulse-chased with 14C-proline. Labeled collagen still appears in the medium, but the secreted protein is digested by pepsin at 20 °C and fails to assemble 67-nm D-banded fibrils. Which molecular explanation is most accurate?

choices.text: Ascorbate is the copper-site reductant for lysyl oxidase, so tropocollagen cannot leave the ER and no labeled protein should appear extracellularly.
Without ascorbate the signal peptide is not cleaved, trapping preprocollagen as an unfolded cytosolic monomer that is never secreted.
Prolyl and lysyl hydroxylases require ascorbate; underhydroxylated chains form thermally labile triple helices that remain pepsin-sensitive and pack poorly into fibrils.
Ascorbate is required only to N-glycosylate asparagines; without sugar, calnexin retains all collagen indefinitely, contradicting the appearance of medium label.

items.explanation: Vitamin C keeps the nonheme iron of prolyl and lysyl hydroxylases in the active Fe2+ state so that X-Y-Gly repeats can be hydroxylated in the ER. Hydroxyproline stabilizes the triple helix by hydrogen bonding and stereoelectronic effects, raising the melting temperature above 37 °C. In ascorbate deficiency the chains remain underhydroxylated, helices unravel near room temperature, pepsin gains access, and D-period packing fails. Secretion is not absolutely blocked, which is why pulse label still reaches the medium. Lysyl oxidase is a copper enzyme that acts after secretion; signal-peptide cleavage and calnexin glycoprotein quality control do not explain pepsin-labile secreted collagen.

distractorRationales.A: Lysyl oxidase is extracellular and copper-dependent; it is not the ascorbate step that thermally destabilizes newly secreted collagen, and the stem shows that labeled protein is secreted.
distractorRationales.B: Signal-peptidase cleavage does not require ascorbate, and a cytosolic trap would prevent any medium label.
distractorRationales.D: Collagen hydroxylation, not N-glycosylation of asparagine, is the ascorbate-dependent modification; calnexin retention would also prevent secretion of labeled chains.

items.stem: A rural county has the state’s highest diabetes prevalence and amputation rate and the fewest endocrinologists and diabetes educators per capita. Tudor Hart’s inverse care law names which relationship?

choices.text: The availability of good medical care tends to vary inversely with the need of the population served
Care is always proportional to need in market systems, so the county is a measurement error
Only individual prejudice by named endocrinologists can produce a shortage
Whitehall already proved rurality is protective, contradicting the amputation rate

items.explanation: Hart’s inverse care law (1971) states that good medical care is least available where it is most needed, especially where market forces dominate. High-need, low-supply counties are the illustration. It is an empirical regularity about distribution, not a claim that measurement must be wrong. Institutional and market allocation can produce shortages without a single prejudiced specialist. Whitehall is an occupational-grade gradient in Britain, not a finding that rural high-need areas are protected.

items.stem: A resting primary oocyte in a primordial follicle has completed premeiotic S phase and is arrested with homologous chromosomes paired as bivalents. The meiotic stage of this oocyte is:

A PCR is designed to amplify a 500 bp genomic target. After 25 cycles, 10 µL of each reaction is run on an agarose gel beside a 100 bp ladder (bands 100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600 bp).

Lane | template | result
1 | 10 ng genomic DNA | single band aligned with the 500 bp ladder mark
2 | water, no DNA | no band
3 | genomic DNA, no polymerase | no band
4 | genomic DNA, annealing temperature 10 °C too low | smear plus extra bands at 300 and 700 bp
5 | water, but a 500 bp band appears

Which quality-control reading is justified?

choices.text: Lane 1 is the expected specific product; lane 2 is a clean negative; lane 5 indicates contamination of the no-template control; lane 4 shows non-specific priming
Lane 5 proves the water contained the 500 bp gene as a natural solute
Lane 3 should have shown a 500 bp band because DNA was added, so polymerase is unnecessary
Lane 1’s alignment with 500 bp proves the sequence is correct to the nucleotide

items.explanation: A unique 500 bp amplicon with a blank no-template lane is the textbook pass. Lane 3 without polymerase cannot synthesise DNA, so a blank lane is the correct enzyme control, not a failure. Extra bands when annealing is too cold are misprimed products. A 500 bp band in a water lane means template (or amplicon) contaminated that tube, the most important fail. Water does not come with genomic targets at PCR-detectable concentration in a well-run lab. Co-migration with a 500 bp marker estimates length, not sequence identity.

distractorRationales.B: A band in the water lane is contamination, not evidence that solvent water encodes a 500 bp gene.
distractorRationales.C: Polymerase is required to extend primers; lane 3 is correctly blank.
distractorRationales.D: Gel mobility gives approximate length; sequencing or a restriction digest would be needed for sequence confirmation.

passage.title: Chiral Chromatography of Arylpropionic Acid Analogs
passage.body:
A fictional arylpropionic acid, compound C, has two enantiomers labeled R-C and S-C. The carboxylic acid group has pKa = 4.4. A chiral stationary phase contains hydrophobic binding pockets and protonated amine sites. Neutral analytes interact mainly through hydrophobic contacts, while carboxylate forms can also interact electrostatically. Very high salt concentrations can screen electrostatic interactions. An achiral column cannot directly distinguish enantiomers unless the compounds are converted into diastereomeric derivatives or salts.

Chromatographic performance under different conditions.
Condition | Column type | Mobile phase pH | Salt level | Retention time R-C (min) | Retention time S-C (min) | Resolution
1 | Achiral silica | 2.5 | low | 5.1 | 5.1 | 0.0
2 | Chiral | 2.5 | low | 6.2 | 7.0 | 1.1
3 | Chiral | 7.5 | low | 12.8 | 16.4 | 2.4
4 | Chiral | 7.5 | high | 8.0 | 9.0 | 0.8
5 | Chiral | 9.5 | low | 13.0 | 16.2 | 2.3

Peak areas for a mixture analyzed under Condition 3.
Peak identity | Peak area
R-C | 300
S-C | 100

Conceptual chiral recognition model. — One enantiomer fits more deeply into the chiral pocket while simultaneously orienting its carboxylate toward a protonated amine site. The other enantiomer has a less favorable alignment and elutes earlier.

items.stem: A mainland bird population is reduced to 12 individuals by a hurricane, then recovers numerically. Neutral heterozygosity and allelic richness remain far below pre-crash values for many generations despite random mating and no detectable change in relative fitness among remaining genotypes. Which process best explains the genetic outcome?

choices.text: A population bottleneck caused genetic drift that lost or fixed alleles; subsequent growth does not restore diversity until mutation or migration replenishes it.
Directional selection favored homozygotes during the storm, and that selection continues to purge heterozygotes after recovery.
Gene flow from a divergent island population immediately restored heterozygosity, which contradicts the persistently low diversity.
Heterozygote advantage intensified during the crash, which would raise, not lower, heterozygosity at the affected loci.

items.explanation: A sharp reduction in census size samples only a few genomes. Alleles are lost or fixed by chance (drift), lowering heterozygosity and allelic richness at neutral loci. When the population later expands, it still carries only the gene pool of the survivors; random mating among them does not recreate lost alleles. Mutation and migration restore diversity only slowly, matching the long-lasting deficit. The stem states that relative fitness among remaining genotypes did not change, so ongoing selection against heterozygotes is unsupported. Gene flow or heterozygote advantage would not leave diversity depressed for generations after numerical recovery.

distractorRationales.B: The stem specifies no fitness differences among remaining genotypes and a deficit at neutral diversity measures, which is drift after a bottleneck, not continued directional selection.
distractorRationales.C: Immigration would introduce alleles and raise heterozygosity; the observation is that diversity stayed low.
distractorRationales.D: Heterozygote advantage maintains polymorphism; it does not explain a crash-associated, lasting loss of allelic richness.

High cortisol should suppress ACTH; if ACTH is nevertheless low (R), the cortisol source is ACTH-independent (adrenal adenoma or exogenous steroid). High cortisol with unsuppressed ACTH (S) is ACTH-dependent hypercortisolism. High ACTH is the opposite of pituitary failure; high cortisol is the opposite of Addison disease.

distractorRationales.A: Pituitary failure lowers ACTH; patient P has ACTH 40 pM, an appropriate response to low cortisol.
distractorRationales.B: Primary adrenal failure lowers cortisol; R has cortisol 900 nM.
distractorRationales.C: Addison disease is cortisol deficiency; S has cortisol 900 nM with high ACTH, i.e. Cushing physiology.

items.stem: A first-episode psychosis service notes that a D2-blocking typical antipsychotic reduces auditory hallucinations and a dopamine agonist for restless legs briefly worsened them. Negative symptoms and cognition barely change. The classical dopamine hypothesis of schizophrenia most directly explains which part of this pattern?

choices.text: Positive symptoms as mesolimbic hyperdopaminergia, which D2 blockade can blunt
Negative symptoms as the primary D2-excess state, which is why they melted away
The entire syndrome as a pure acetylcholine deficit, as in Alzheimer disease
Parkinsonism of the substantia nigra as the cause of hallucinations

items.explanation: The classical dopamine hypothesis ties positive psychotic symptoms to excess mesolimbic D2 signaling; typical neuroleptics are D2 antagonists, and agonists can aggravate psychosis. Negative and cognitive symptoms are less well explained by that simple excess and may relate to prefrontal hypodopaminergia or NMDA hypofunction—hence their persistence. Alzheimer disease is a cholinergic/cortical-degeneration story. Nigrostriatal dopamine loss causes Parkinsonism, a side effect of typicals, not the source of the hallucinations.

distractorRationales.B: Negative symptoms are not the symptoms that typical D2 blockers reliably erase.
distractorRationales.C: Alzheimer’s cholinergic deficit is a different disease model.
distractorRationales.D: Nigrostriatal loss produces Parkinsonism, not the core hallucinatory syndrome of schizophrenia.

items.stem: A covalent inhibitor modifies an essential active-site residue in 30% of enzyme molecules. After excess inhibitor is removed by dialysis, activity remains 70% of the original value. Which kinetic effect is most likely when substrate is varied?

choices.text: Vmax decreases, while the Km of the remaining active enzyme is largely unchanged.
The enzyme becomes positively cooperative even if it was monomeric.
Km increases, while Vmax remains unchanged.
Both Km and Vmax increase because dialysis activates the enzyme.

items.explanation: Irreversible inactivation reduces the concentration of active enzyme molecules. This lowers Vmax, which depends on active enzyme concentration, while the substrate affinity of the remaining unmodified enzyme molecules can remain approximately the same. Common miss: Treating irreversible inhibition as though it must change substrate affinity of the remaining active enzyme. This is the expected effect of reducing active enzyme concentration. Source: OpenMCAT (AGPL-3.0). Unverified AI practice; not AAMC.

distractorRationales.B: Irreversible modification does not by itself create cooperativity in a monomeric enzyme.
distractorRationales.C: This pattern is typical of competitive inhibition, not irreversible loss of enzyme molecules.
distractorRationales.D: Dialysis removes free inhibitor but does not reverse covalent modification in the stem.

items.stem: A patient is deficient in pyridoxal phosphate. Amino-acid catabolism that funnels nitrogen into glutamate is impaired. Which reaction class is most directly affected?

choices.text: Oxidative deamination of glutamate by glutamate dehydrogenase, which uses NAD(P)+ rather than PLP
Transamination (for example alanine aminotransferase) that transfers an amino group to α-ketoglutarate
Carbamoyl phosphate synthesis, which requires biotin as the prosthetic group
Peptide-bond hydrolysis by proteases, which depends on zinc or serine catalysis rather than PLP

items.explanation: Aminotransferases use pyridoxal phosphate to transfer an amino group from an amino acid to an α-keto acid, most often producing glutamate from α-ketoglutarate. Without PLP, this funneling of nitrogen into glutamate is blocked, matching the clinical stem. Glutamate dehydrogenase then can release ammonia from glutamate, but GDH uses NAD(P)+ and does not require PLP, so it is not the primary PLP-deficient step. CPS-I uses ammonia, ATP, and N-acetylglutamate, not biotin (biotin is on carboxylases such as pyruvate carboxylase). Proteases break peptide bonds by unrelated mechanisms and would not specifically stall nitrogen funneling into glutamate.

distractorRationales.A: Glutamate dehydrogenase is a PLP-independent NAD(P)+-linked oxidative deamination. It would not be the first casualty of isolated PLP deficiency in this funneling pathway.
distractorRationales.C: CPS-I does not use PLP or biotin. Biotin is the cofactor of carboxylases, so this choice misidentifies both the enzyme class and the missing cofactor.
distractorRationales.D: Proteases hydrolyze peptide bonds and do not require PLP; they also do not funnel free amino-acid nitrogen into glutamate as transaminases do.

items.stem: A child with vitamin D deficiency has low intestinal Ca2+ and phosphate absorption, secondary hyperparathyroidism, and poorly mineralized osteoid at growth plates (rickets). The organic matrix that fails to mineralize adequately is composed primarily of:

choices.text: Hydroxyapatite crystals with no protein scaffold
Pure elastin, which is the tensile protein of bone osteoid
Type I collagen osteoid, which normally nucleates hydroxyapatite mineral

items.explanation: Bone is a composite: type I collagen and ground substance (osteoid) deposited by osteoblasts, later mineralized with hydroxyapatite. In rickets/osteomalacia the scaffold is laid down but calcium-phosphate product is insufficient for proper mineralization, so unmineralized osteoid accumulates and bones are soft. Hydroxyapatite is the mineral, not the organic matrix. Elastin is important in ligaments and skin, not the bulk of bone osteoid. Glycogen is not the secreted bone matrix. Vitamin D's role here is mineral supply (and PTH-driven wasting of phosphate), not a switch from collagen to elastin.

distractorRationales.A: Hydroxyapatite is the missing mineral, not the organic osteoid that is overabundant in rickets.
distractorRationales.B: Osteoblasts do not build osteoid from glycogen.
distractorRationales.C: Bone tensile protein is type I collagen, not elastin.

items.stem: In the fed state, acetyl-CoA carboxylase is active and malonyl-CoA is abundant in hepatocytes. Fatty acyl-CoAs are generated in the cytosol, yet mitochondrial β-oxidation is slow. Which mechanism best explains the block?

choices.text: Malonyl-CoA inhibits carnitine palmitoyltransferase I, preventing acyl transfer into the matrix.
Malonyl-CoA activates pyruvate dehydrogenase, consuming all available carnitine.
Malonyl-CoA is the substrate of thiolase, which reverses β-oxidation in the matrix.
Carnitine is consumed as a cofactor of fatty acid synthase, leaving none for the shuttle.

items.explanation: Long-chain acyl-CoAs cannot cross the inner mitochondrial membrane. Carnitine palmitoyltransferase I on the outer membrane transfers the acyl group to carnitine, and the acylcarnitine is shuttled into the matrix. Malonyl-CoA, the committed product of acetyl-CoA carboxylase during fatty-acid synthesis, allosterically inhibits CPT-I. In the fed state this prevents newly made or dietary fatty acyl-CoAs from being immediately oxidized, avoiding a futile cycle. Malonyl-CoA does not activate PDH to burn carnitine, is not a thiolase substrate that reverses β-oxidation, and is not consumed by FAS in place of NADPH and acetyl/malonyl-ACP. The CPT-I gate is the standard reciprocal regulation.

distractorRationales.B: Malonyl-CoA does not activate PDH, and PDH does not consume carnitine. PDH is a carbohydrate-to-acetyl-CoA enzyme, not the β-oxidation gate.
distractorRationales.C: Thiolase in β-oxidation uses 3-ketoacyl-CoA, not malonyl-CoA. Malonyl-CoA is a cytosolic building block for fatty-acid synthesis, not a matrix substrate that runs the spiral backward.
distractorRationales.D: Fatty acid synthase uses acetyl-CoA/malonyl-CoA on ACP and NADPH; carnitine is not a stoichiometric FAS cofactor, so FAS does not deplete the shuttle that way.

passage.title: psg-cp-7
passage.body:
The physical properties of a substance are set largely by the forces between its molecules. Consider a data set the students assemble. Among the hydrides of Group 16, hydrogen sulfide (H2S) boils at -60 C, yet water (H2O), a lighter molecule, boils at +100 C - a striking exception to the usual trend that heavier molecules boil higher. The students also compare two compounds with the identical formula C2H6O: ethanol, which boils at 78 C, and dimethyl ether, which boils at -24 C. Finally, they tabulate the boiling points of the noble gases and find a steady rise from helium through xenon.
To interpret the data they review molecular structure. Oxygen is far more electronegative than hydrogen, so each O-H bond is polar; in water the two O-H bonds and two lone pairs on oxygen arrange the electron domains tetrahedrally, giving the molecule a bent shape with an H-O-H angle near 104.5 degrees and a net dipole moment. They classify the intermolecular forces available to each substance: London dispersion forces (present in all molecules, stronger in larger and more polarizable electron clouds), dipole-dipole forces (between permanent dipoles), and hydrogen bonding (the especially strong attraction when H bonded to N, O, or F is drawn to a lone pair on another such atom).
Their goal is to connect each measured boiling point to the strongest intermolecular force a molecule can form, and to explain the anomalies - water's high boiling point, ethanol versus its isomer, and the noble-gas trend - in terms of hydrogen bonding, polarity, geometry, and polarizability.

items.stem:
Relative rates of reaction with 0.10 M NaOH in ethanol/water at 25 °C:

Substrate | relative rate | rate law observed
CH3Br | 1200 | rate = k[substrate][OH−]
CH3CH2Br | 80 | rate = k[substrate][OH−]
(CH3)2CHBr | 3 | mixed
(CH3)3CBr | 0.01 in this bimolecular test; fast in polar protic solvent without needing [OH−] | rate = k[substrate] in water

Which mechanistic reading is supported?

choices.text: All four follow the same rate law, so the mechanism never changes
Methyl bromide is slowest because it is the least hindered
Primary substrates favour SN2 (second-order, fastest at CH3); tertiary favours SN1 (first-order, independent of [OH−])
Tertiary is fastest at SN2 because three methyl groups donate electrons to the pentavalent carbon

items.explanation: The second-order law and the 1200 → 80 → 3 fall as alkyl substitution increases are the SN2 steric series, fastest at methyl. tert-Butyl bromide is near-zero under bimolecular conditions but reacts by a first-order law in water, the SN1 ionisation route available to a tertiary carbocation. Electron donation would, if anything, help SN1, not SN2; the table shows tertiary is slowest in the bimolecular column. Rate laws are not all the same. Least hindered CH3Br is the fastest SN2 substrate, not the slowest.

distractorRationales.A: Methyl and ethyl are second-order; tertiary in water is first-order.
distractorRationales.B: CH3Br has relative rate 1200, the maximum in the SN2 series.
distractorRationales.D: The SN2 column lists (CH3)3CBr at 0.01, the slowest, because the backside is blocked.

items.stem: Hepatocytes are treated with a protonophore that dissipates the inner-mitochondrial-membrane proton gradient without chemically destroying electron-transport complexes. The expected immediate result is:

choices.text: ATP synthesis rises and O2 consumption falls
ATP synthesis falls while O2 consumption continues or increases
electron transport stops because the complexes are irreversibly denatured
the outer mitochondrial membrane dissolves, releasing all matrix enzymes to the cytosol

items.explanation: ATP synthase requires the proton-motive force to drive phosphorylation. A protonophore lets H+ re-enter the matrix without passing through ATP synthase, so ATP production falls. Electron transport is no longer opposed by a steep gradient, so respiration (O2 use as the terminal acceptor) typically continues or accelerates and energy is lost as heat. Uncouplers are not general denaturants, and they do not specifically lyse the outer membrane.

distractorRationales.A: This is the opposite of uncoupling. Blocking respiration (for example with cyanide) lowers O2 use; uncoupling does not raise ATP yield.
distractorRationales.C: The stem states that complexes are not destroyed. Uncoupling severs the gradient, not the hardware of the chain.
distractorRationales.D: Outer-membrane rupture is a different pathology (for example MOMP in apoptosis), not the definition of a protonophore.

items.stem: A 2 kg object starts from rest. A net force does 100 J of work on it. The object's speed after that work is done is:
items.explanation: The work–energy theorem states that net work equals the change in kinetic energy. The object starts at rest, so W_net = (1/2) m v^2 = 100 J. With m = 2 kg this is (1/2)(2) v^2 = v^2 = 100, hence v = 10 m/s. The mass factor 1/2 m equals 1 kg, so the speed in m/s is simply the square root of the work in joules. Forgetting the 1/2 or treating KE as m v rather than (1/2) m v^2 produces the slower distractors.

distractorRationales.A: This is W/m divided by something extra, or v = sqrt(W/m)/sqrt(2). Solving (1/2) m v^2 = 100 with m = 2 kg does not yield 5 m/s.
distractorRationales.B: This is about sqrt(50), which appears if KE is taken as m v^2 without the 1/2: 2 v^2 = 100 gives v = sqrt(50) ≈ 7 m/s.
distractorRationales.D: This is W/m = 50, as if work were equal to m v or to m a with a confused for v. Energy has a squared speed, so the square root is required.

passage.title: psg-bb-5
passage.body:
To probe how mitochondria couple fuel oxidation to ATP synthesis, researchers suspended isolated mitochondria in a buffered chamber fitted with an oxygen electrode, so that the rate of oxygen consumption could be followed continuously. Because the electron transport chain uses O2 as its final electron acceptor, oxygen consumption serves as a readout of electron flow.
The team added an oxidizable substrate (to feed electrons into the chain) plus ADP and inorganic phosphate (the raw materials for ATP synthesis). Oxygen consumption rose to a brisk, steady rate, and ATP accumulated in the chamber. They then added oligomycin, a compound that blocks the proton channel of ATP synthase. Oxygen consumption fell almost to zero, and ATP synthesis stopped. Finally, they added 2,4-dinitrophenol (DNP), a small molecule that ferries protons across the inner mitochondrial membrane. Oxygen consumption surged back to a high rate, yet no ATP was produced; the released energy instead appeared as heat.
The investigators explained the pattern in terms of the proton-motive force. Electron transport pumps protons from the matrix into the intermembrane space, building an electrochemical gradient; ATP synthase normally lets those protons flow back into the matrix, harnessing the gradient to make ATP. Blocking ATP synthase lets the gradient build until it opposes further pumping, so electron flow (and O2 use) slows. A protonophore like DNP short-circuits the gradient, so electron transport races ahead while its energy is dissipated as heat rather than captured as ATP.

items.stem: In a Robbers Cave-style camp, two cabin groups become hostile during tournaments. Eating together does not help. Repairing a shared water tank that neither cabin can fix alone reduces hostility. Sherif’s realistic-conflict account plus the later contact hypothesis most directly credits which ingredient?

choices.text: Mere proximity, which Allport said is sufficient by itself
Scapegoating as in Dollard’s frustration–aggression theory, which predicts more hostility after the tank is fixed
Superordinate goals that create interdependence, plus contact under cooperative, equal-status conditions
Goffman’s front-stage manners, which dissolve prejudice without changing goals

items.explanation: Sherif’s realistic conflict theory says competition for scarce prizes produces intergroup hostility; superordinate goals that require cooperation reduce it. Allport’s contact hypothesis adds that contact works when it is equal-status, cooperative, and supported by norms—not mere cafeteria proximity, which failed at Robbers Cave. Frustration–aggression/scapegoating would not uniquely predict the tank’s success. Dramaturgy is impression management, not the named conflict-reduction mechanism.

distractorRationales.A: Mere contact without cooperation failed in Sherif’s study and is not Allport’s full recipe.
distractorRationales.B: Fixing the tank reduced, rather than increased, hostility, opposite a simple scapegoat prediction.
distractorRationales.D: Goffman does not replace Sherif’s superordinate-goal finding.

items.stem: Which of the following best captures the author's primary purpose?

choices.text: To prove that all censuses should be abolished because counting is inherently a form of wartime extraction.

passage.title: The census of the uncounted
passage.body:
Political arithmetic began as a courtly hobby: a way of estimating how many subjects a prince could tax, feed, or send to war. Its early practitioners treated people as a kind of harvest. What could be enumerated could be extracted. What could not be enumerated was, for administrative purposes, a rumor.

The modern census inherited the appetite and dressed it as representation. To be counted is now advertised as a civic right, a way of appearing in the distribution of schools, clinics, and parliamentary seats. The advertisement is not false. Under-counted neighborhoods do lose clinics. The advertisement is incomplete. A census is also a machine for deciding which kinds of life will be treated as facts and which will remain anecdotes told to a volunteer with a clipboard.

Consider the category. Every census must invent boxes. The boxes are not discovered in nature; they are negotiated among ministries, churches, and, later, identity movements. A person who lives in two houses, or in none, or who works in a language the form does not print, must be forced into a box or dropped. Dropping looks like a clerical mishap. It is often a theory of the state: some lives are too expensive to verify, too mobile to locate, too politically inconvenient to add to a total that will be used against the ministry next year.

Statisticians reply that they already know this, that they publish coverage estimates and post-enumeration surveys, that the professional ethic is to name the error. Naming the error is not the same as refusing the uses of the total. A coverage estimate can become a footnote that licenses the headline number. The public hears fifty million; the appendix whispers that the fifty million is a compromise among several less flattering models. Compromise is not a crime. Treating the compromise as a photograph is.

There is a further twist. Groups that have been historically erased often demand better counting, and they are right to. Visibility in a dataset can be a precondition of funds. Yet the same groups may later discover that a sharper count is also a sharper target: for policing, for debt collection, for the allocation of blame when a service fails. The census does not choose the policy. It does make the policy cheaper to aim.

None of this is an argument for ignorance. A state that refuses to count will invent its numbers in the back room and call the invention common sense. The argument is for a less enchanted relationship to the table. Read the boxes as arguments. Read the missing as a constituency. And when a politician says the numbers speak for themselves, notice that speech is exactly what numbers cannot do until someone supplies a sentence.

passage.title: psg-cars-1
passage.body:
Is there any knowledge in the world so certain that no reasonable person could doubt it? This question, which at first sight might not seem difficult, is really among the most difficult that can be asked. In daily life we assume as certain many things which, on closer scrutiny, are found to be so full of apparent contradictions that only a great deal of thought enables us to know what it is that we may really believe.
Consider the plain table before me. To the eye it appears rectangular, brown, and shiny; to the touch it is smooth, cool, and hard; when I tap it, it gives out a wooden sound. Anyone else who sees, feels, and hears the table will agree with this description, so it might seem that no difficulty could arise. But the moment we try to be more precise, our troubles begin. Although I believe that the table is 'really' of one uniform brown, the parts that reflect the light look far brighter than the rest, and some parts look white because of reflected light. If I move, the parts that reflect the light change, so that the apparent distribution of colours upon the table shifts. It follows that if several people look at the table at the same moment, no two of them will see exactly the same distribution of colours, for no two can view it from precisely the same point, and any change in the point of view changes the way in which the light is reflected.
For most practical purposes these differences are unimportant, but to the painter they are all-important: the painter has to unlearn the habit of thinking that things seem to have the colour which common sense says they 'really' have, and to learn the habit of seeing things as they appear. Here we already meet with one of the distinctions that cause the most trouble in philosophy — the distinction between 'appearance' and 'reality,' between what things seem to be and what they are. The table, if it is 'real' at all, must have some real colour; yet the colour we see is not a property of the table in itself but something depending upon the table, the observer, and the way the light falls. When, in ordinary life, we speak of the colour of the table, we mean only the sort of colour which it will seem to have to a normal spectator, under ordinary conditions of light, from an ordinary point of view. But the other colours which appear under other conditions have just as good a right to be considered real; and so, to avoid favouritism, we are compelled to deny that the table has any one particular colour.
The same holds for the texture. With the naked eye the grain of the wood looks smooth and even; under a microscope it shows roughness, and hills and valleys, and all sorts of differences that are imperceptible to unaided sight. Which of these is the 'real' table? We are naturally tempted to say that what we see through the microscope is more real; yet a still more powerful instrument would reveal something different again, so that we can never rest content with what the eye alone reports. Thus confidence in the senses, which had seemed so secure, begins to desert us.
It becomes evident that the real table, if there is one, is not the same as what we immediately experience by sight or touch or hearing. The real table, if it exists, is not immediately known to us at all, but must be an inference from what is immediately known. Hence two very difficult questions at once arise: Is there a real table at all? And if so, what sort of object can it be?

items.stem:
Paired plasma osmolality and ADH during a water-restriction test:

Plasma osmolality (mOsm kg−1) | ADH (pg mL−1) | urine osmolality (mOsm kg−1)
280 | 1 | 80
290 | 4 | 400
300 | 10 | 900
320 | 12 | 950

ADH insertion of aquaporins in the collecting duct raises urine osmolality. Which description of the feedback loop is best?

choices.text: ADH falls as osmolality rises, producing more dilute urine
Urine is always 900–950 mOsm kg−1, so ADH is unnecessary in this subject
The loop is open-loop feed-forward from urine to plasma, because urine osmolality exceeds plasma
Above about 280 mOsm kg−1, rising plasma osmolality increases ADH, which increases urine concentration; the response saturates near 950 mOsm kg−1

items.explanation: Each row shows plasma osmolality, ADH, and urine concentration rising together from a threshold near 280 mOsm kg−1, the standard osmoreceptor–ADH–kidney negative-feedback cascade that conserves water. The last step from 300 to 320 mOsm kg−1 barely changes urine (900 to 950), i.e. a saturating concentrating ability. ADH does not fall, and urine at 80 mOsm kg−1 when ADH is 1 proves the kidney can dilute when ADH is low. Concentrated urine is the output that corrects plasma osmolality, not evidence that the loop runs from urine to plasma as the sensed variable.

distractorRationales.A: ADH rises 1 → 12 as osmolality rises 280 → 320; urine becomes more concentrated, not more dilute.
distractorRationales.B: The first row has urine 80 mOsm kg−1, so concentration is regulated, not fixed.
distractorRationales.C: The sensed variable listed first is plasma osmolality; concentrated urine is the effector response.

passage.title: On keeping a promise to a stranger
passage.body:
When the magistrate asked why he had returned the purse, the clerk did not say honesty. He said habit. He had been taught, in a household that measured virtue by small repetitions, that a found object remains someone else's until the world has been given a fair chance to reclaim it. The purse contained little money and a letter, unsealed, beginning: I will not be there when you arrive. He did not finish it. To finish it, he thought, would convert a duty into a story, and stories have a way of making the finder important.

Philosophers like to treat this as a puzzle about property and knowledge. If he does not know the owner, is the duty weaker? If the letter would have saved a marriage, does withholding it become a harm? The clerk would have found the questions indecent. He was not refusing knowledge so much as refusing a role. The city had clerks for lost property; it did not have clerks for other people's farewells.

A later commentator, writing after the clerk was dead, praised him as a Kantian saint: he acted from a maxim he could will as universal. The praise is too clean. The clerk's maxim was local and slightly ashamed. He did not want to be the man who had read the letter. Shame, not universality, kept his eyes off the page. That is not a lesser ethics. It is an ethics that knows how quickly curiosity dresses itself as concern.

The owner collected the purse the next morning and did not thank him. In the commentary this becomes a test of whether virtue needs recognition. The clerk, if asked, would have said only that the counter was busy.

passage.title: The museum as a verb
passage.body:
Conservation used to mean stopping time. A painting was a patient; varnish was a bandage; the ideal was to return the object to a single authentic hour and then prevent further hours from occurring. That ideal had a hidden historiography. It assumed the authentic hour was already known, usually as the artist’s last brushstroke, and that later repairs, soot, liturgy, and even damage were noise.

A newer conservation talk prefers verbs. To museum an object is to keep choosing which traces will remain legible. Cleaning is not the removal of history; it is the promotion of one history over another. The nineteenth-century restorer who “completed” a medieval panel was not more ideological than the twenty-first-century restorer who leaves the lacuna as a paler mute. Both are editors. They differ in which audience they imagine and in how proudly they sign the edit.

Critics of reversible methods sometimes complain that visible fills and honest seams break the spell. They want the old miracle: an untouched past that happens to hang at eye level under LEDs. The complaint is aesthetically sincere and philosophically confused. The spell was always produced with scaffolding, attributions, and lighting. Reversibility is not a refusal of beauty. It is a refusal to trap the next generation inside today’s certainty about what the object “really” was.

There is a colonial edge. Objects that arrived by seizure were often cleaned into a style that made them readable as art in the receiving capital, which is to say, cleaned of the uses that had made them un-museumlike. To restore the pigment without restoring the right of refusal is to complete the seizure in a gentler font. Some institutions now consult source communities about smoke, wear, and whether an object should be seen at all. Consultation is slow and can be theater. It is still a different verb from rescue.

If this sounds like relativism, notice what it does not say. It does not say that all edits are equal, or that pigment chemistry is a matter of taste. It says that technical competence cannot supply the missing decision about which past is being kept available. The decision will be made. Calling it science does not make it less a decision. Calling it care does not either. The more honest museum is the one that can show its verbs.

Lungs alter CO2 (fast, via breathing rate); kidneys alter bicarbonate reabsorption/excretion (slow) — together buffering blood pH. Source: Open-MCAT (CC BY-NC 4.0, © 2026 Makenzi L. McDermott). Unverified personal study copy.

distractorRationales.A: Reversed — lungs handle CO2 quickly, kidneys handle bicarbonate slowly.
distractorRationales.B: Liver/spleen aren't the primary acid-base regulators.
distractorRationales.D: Heart/brain don't directly regulate blood pH balance.

items.stem: A solution has a pH of 3. Compared to a solution with pH 5, the pH 3 solution is:

choices.text: Less acidic, with a lower H+ concentration
More acidic, with only 2 times higher H+ concentration
More acidic, with 100 times higher H+ concentration

items.explanation: pH is a log scale: pH = -log10[H+]. Each whole-number drop in pH means a 10-fold increase in H+ concentration. Going from pH 5 to pH 3 is a difference of 2, so H+ concentration is 10^2 = 100 times higher. A common trap: assuming pH differences are linear. Because pH is a log10 scale of H+ concentration, every 1-unit drop means 10x more H+ ions (more acidic), and every 1-unit rise means 10x fewer (more basic/alkaline). Memory tip: "Every step is a 10x leap": pH is a log scale, so each single-unit drop means 10x more H+. Count the gap between the two pH numbers, then raise 10 to that power. Source: gamsat-trainer original practice (not ACER). Unverified.

items.stem: Transection of the pituitary stalk rapidly lowers circulating ADH and produces diabetes insipidus, while prolactin often rises because hypothalamic dopamine can no longer reach the anterior lobe. These findings are consistent with ADH being:

choices.text: Synthesized by anterior-pituitary gonadotrophs and released into the cavernous sinus
A steroid produced by the adrenal cortex under ACTH control only
Synthesized in hypothalamic nuclei and axonally transported to the posterior pituitary for release
Made by ovarian granulosa cells as the primary osmoregulatory hormone

items.explanation: ADH (vasopressin) and oxytocin are peptides synthesized in hypothalamic magnocellular neurons (supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei). Axons of the hypothalamo-hypophyseal tract terminate in the posterior pituitary, so cutting the stalk disconnects those endings from their somata and ADH falls. Anterior-lobe hormones are made by pituitary cells under hypothalamic releasing/inhibiting factors delivered by the portal system; loss of dopamine inhibition explains the prolactin rise and shows the stalk lesion is not a generic shutdown of every pituitary cell. ADH is not an adrenal steroid or an ovarian product.

distractorRationales.A: Gonadotrophs secrete LH/FSH, not ADH; ADH is posterior-pituitary/hypothalamic.
distractorRationales.B: Adrenal steroids are cortisol/aldosterone/androgens, not ADH.
distractorRationales.D: The ovary does not secrete the physiologic antidiuretic hormone.

items.stem: The same acetic acid sample (25.0 mL of 0.10 M; pKa = 4.74) is titrated with 0.10 M NaOH. After 12.5 mL of NaOH has been added, the pH is closest to:
items.explanation: Initial millimoles of acetic acid = 2.50. After 12.5 mL of 0.10 M NaOH, 1.25 mmol of HA has been converted to acetate, leaving 1.25 mmol HA. That is the half-equivalence point, where [HA] = [A−] (volumes cancel in the ratio). Henderson–Hasselbalch then gives pH = pKa = 4.74. 2.87 is the approximate starting pH of 0.10 M acetic acid before any base. 7.00 would be a strong-acid equivalence point. 8.72 is the ballpark equivalence pH after a full 25.0 mL of NaOH, not after half that volume.

distractorRationales.B: 2.87 estimates the pH of untitrated 0.10 M acetic acid (√(Ka C)), not the half-neutralized buffer.
distractorRationales.C: pH 7 is not a special point on a weak-acid titration curve except by coincidence; half-equivalence is at pKa.
distractorRationales.D: ≈8.7 is the equivalence-point pH after 25.0 mL of NaOH, when the solute is acetate alone.

items.stem: Hydrogen is burned: 2 H2 + O2 → 2 H2O. A closed bulb is charged with 4.0 g H2 (Mr = 2.0) and 16 g O2 (Mr = 32). Which reagent limits, and what mass of water can form?

choices.text: The reagents are stoichiometric; 20 g H2O forms (4 + 16)
O2 limits (0.50 mol); 9.0 g H2O forms
O2 limits (0.50 mol); 18 g H2O forms
H2 limits (2.0 mol); 36 g H2O forms

items.explanation: Moles: n(H2) = 4.0/2.0 = 2.0 mol; n(O2) = 16/32 = 0.50 mol. The equation consumes 2 mol H2 per 1 mol O2, so 0.50 mol O2 would need 1.0 mol H2 and is limiting; 1.0 mol H2 remains unused. Water produced is 2 mol H2O per mol O2, hence 1.0 mol = 18 g. Hydrogen is in excess, not limiting. Adding masses of H2 and O2 (20 g) ignores that 2.0 g of unused H2 stays uncombined. Half of 18 g would be appropriate for 0.25 mol O2, not 0.50 mol.

distractorRationales.A: The mole ratio is 2.0 : 0.50 = 4 : 1, not the stoichiometric 2 : 1, and unused H2 is not water.
distractorRationales.B: 0.50 mol O2 produces 1.0 mol H2O = 18 g, not 0.50 mol = 9 g.
distractorRationales.D: 2.0 mol H2 would require 1.0 mol O2; only 0.50 mol O2 is present, so H2 is excess.

items.stem: Acetone (CH3COCH3, bp 56 °C) and 2-propanol (CH3CH(OH)CH3, bp 82 °C) have similar molar masses. Why is the alcohol’s boiling point higher?

choices.text: Acetone is more polar, so it should boil higher; the alcohol’s higher boiling point is due to its slightly larger mass alone.
2-Propanol can donate and accept hydrogen bonds, whereas acetone can only accept hydrogen bonds and otherwise relies on dipole–dipole and London forces between ketone molecules.
Acetone ionizes in the liquid, lowering its boiling point.
The C=O bond of acetone is stronger than the C–O bond of the alcohol, so acetone molecules are harder to separate.

items.explanation: Boiling separates molecules, so intermolecular forces—not intramolecular bond strengths—set the boiling point. 2-Propanol has an O–H group and therefore hydrogen-bonds to itself. Acetone is polar and can accept a hydrogen bond from a donor, but a pair of acetone molecules cannot form O–H···O hydrogen bonds. The extra cohesion in the alcohol raises its boiling point despite nearly identical molar mass. Acetone does not ionize as a bulk liquid, and the strong C=O covalent bond is not broken on vaporization.

distractorRationales.A: Acetone is polar but lacks an H-bond donor. The boiling-point gap is much larger than the tiny mass difference would suggest.
distractorRationales.C: Acetone is a molecular liquid; it does not dissociate into ions in the neat liquid in a way that would control boiling point.
distractorRationales.D: Vaporization does not break the carbonyl double bond. Intramolecular bond strength is the wrong comparison.

items.stem: A full-thickness burn destroys epidermis including the stratum corneum. Insensible water loss and infection risk both rise sharply. The most direct explanation is loss of:

choices.text: Dermal melanin production, which is the primary water-tight seal of skin
The cornified lipid-keratin barrier that limits transepidermal water loss and microbial invasion
Vitamin D photoproduction, which is what physically occludes bacteria
Eccrine overproduction of hypotonic fluid as the only change after a burn

items.explanation: The stratum corneum is a brick-and-mortar of keratinized corneocytes and intercellular lipids from lamellar bodies. That composite is the principal barrier to evaporative water loss and to many microbes. Destroying it in a full-thickness burn is why patients desiccate and become infected unless the surface is replaced or dressed. Melanin absorbs UV in deeper living layers; it is not the water seal. Cutaneous vitamin D synthesis is a photochemical reaction, not a mechanical lid on bacteria. Burned skin does not cool the patient by secreting extra sweat from destroyed glands; insensible loss is barrier failure, not eccrine overdrive.

distractorRationales.A: Melanin is a UV pigment transferred to keratinocytes, not the lipid-keratin water barrier.
distractorRationales.C: Vitamin D is a hormone precursor, not the physical occlusion that keeps water in and pathogens out.
distractorRationales.D: Full-thickness injury destroys sweat glands; the water loss is passive through a missing barrier.

items.stem:
Human red cells have an internal osmolarity of 300 mOsm. Equal aliquots are placed in NaCl baths (NaCl treated as membrane-impermeant). Relative cell volume at 2 min is:
150 mOsm bath: 1.82; 300 mOsm: 1.00; 450 mOsm: 0.71; 600 mOsm: 0.58.
Which description matches the data and osmosis?

choices.text: Cells swell in the hypotonic 150 mOsm bath and shrink in the hypertonic 450 and 600 mOsm baths.
150 mOsm is hypertonic, because the volume 1.82 shows water leaving the cells.
Volume is independent of bath osmolarity, because 0.58 is not far from 1.82.
600 mOsm causes lysis; lysis would increase, not decrease, packed cell volume.

items.explanation: Water moves toward the higher osmolarity. At 150 mOsm the bath is hypotonic to 300 mOsm cytoplasm, so water enters and relative volume rises to 1.82 (less than the ideal 300/150 = 2 because of non-solvent cell solids). At 300 mOsm there is no net driving force (volume 1.00). At 450 and 600 mOsm the bath is hypertonic, water leaves, and volume falls to 0.71 and 0.58, near the ideal 300/450 = 0.67 and 300/600 = 0.50. A volume below 1 is shrinkage, not lysis.

distractorRationales.B: Volume 1.82 is swelling from water entry; 150 mOsm is hypotonic, not hypertonic.
distractorRationales.C: Volume falls monotonically from 1.82 to 0.58 as osmolarity rises from 150 to 600 mOsm.
distractorRationales.D: Lysis would burst cells and cannot explain a relative volume of 0.58; that is crenation in a hypertonic bath.

items.stem: Which alternative explanation for the memory findings is most directly weakened by Table 2?

choices.text: The restricted-sleep group experienced greater fatigue than the normal-sleep group.
The cued-recall test provided retrieval cues.
The restricted-sleep group was much less motivated than the normal-sleep group.
The sleep manipulation affected working memory.

items.explanation: Motivation ratings were similar across groups: 5.8 in the normal-sleep group and 5.6 in the restricted-sleep group. This weakens the claim that lower performance was primarily due to substantially lower motivation in the restricted-sleep group. Common miss: Assuming any self-report difference is a confound instead of checking the direction and size of the reported values. This is correct. The motivation scores are nearly the same, so motivation differences are unlikely to fully explain the performance gap. Source: OpenMCAT (AGPL-3.0). Unverified AI practice; not AAMC.

distractorRationales.A: Table 2 supports, rather than weakens, greater fatigue in the restricted-sleep group.
distractorRationales.B: The existence of retrieval cues is part of the task structure, not an alternative explanation weakened by motivation and fatigue data.
distractorRationales.D: The 2-back results are consistent with an effect on working memory, not weakened by Table 2.

passage.title: Working Memory, Sleep Restriction, and Retrieval Cues
passage.body:
A fictional laboratory study examined how one night of sleep restriction affects memory performance. Participants were randomly assigned to either a normal-sleep group or a restricted-sleep group. The next morning, all participants studied 30 neutral word pairs. After a 20-minute filler task, they completed two tests. In the free-recall test, participants wrote down as many target words as possible. In the cued-recall test, participants were shown the first word of each pair and attempted to retrieve the associated target word. Participants also completed a 2-back task as a measure of working memory updating.

Memory and working-memory performance
Group | Free recall: mean words recalled | Cued recall: mean words recalled | 2-back accuracy (%)
Normal sleep | 18.4 | 24.1 | 87
Restricted sleep | 13.2 | 20.2 | 73

Self-reported fatigue and motivation
Group | Fatigue rating, 1 to 7 | Motivation rating, 1 to 7
Normal sleep | 2.3 | 5.8
Restricted sleep | 5.9 | 5.6

Retrieval benefit — Both groups recalled more words on cued recall than on free recall, but the restricted-sleep group performed worse than the normal-sleep group on both tests.

items.stem: Acetyl-CoA labeled in both carbon atoms of the acetyl group enters the citric acid cycle by condensing with unlabeled oxaloacetate. After one complete turn, regenerating a four-carbon intermediate, how many of those labeled carbons have been released as CO2?

choices.text: Zero; the two CO2 molecules lost in that turn come from carboxyl groups that were already on oxaloacetate.
One; isocitrate dehydrogenase always releases the methyl carbon of the newly added acetyl group.
Two; both acetyl carbons are fully oxidized to CO2 before succinate is formed.
Three; an extra CO2 is released at succinyl-CoA synthetase.

items.explanation: Citrate synthase adds the two carbons of acetyl-CoA to oxaloacetate. In the same turn, isocitrate dehydrogenase and α-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase each release one CO2, but those carboxyl carbons originated in the oxaloacetate that accepted the acetyl group, not in the acetyl group just added. Both labeled carbons remain in succinate (and therefore in the regenerated four-carbon acids). Because succinate is symmetric, those labels scramble and a fraction of the label is lost in subsequent turns, but the first turn releases none of the acetyl carbons as CO2. Succinyl-CoA synthetase does not decarboxylate.

distractorRationales.B: Isocitrate dehydrogenase does not specifically release the methyl carbon of the acetyl group in the first turn; that methyl carbon remains in the four-carbon intermediates.
distractorRationales.C: Neither acetyl carbon is lost as CO2 in the first turn. Both are still present in succinate, so the ‘fully oxidized before succinate’ claim is false.
distractorRationales.D: Succinyl-CoA synthetase converts succinyl-CoA to succinate with formation of GTP; it does not release CO2, and three labeled CO2 molecules are not produced in one turn.

items.stem: Why does decreasing the external load resistance from 500 ohm to 250 ohm produce only a small increase in current from Trial C to Trial D?

choices.text: The battery is approaching a current-limited regime because internal resistance and electrode polarization reduce terminal voltage.
Ohm's law requires current to decrease whenever resistance decreases.
The standard cell potential becomes negative at lower resistance.
The external resistor prevents any oxygen reduction from occurring.

items.explanation: If the cell behaved like an ideal constant-voltage source, halving the load resistance would approximately double current. Instead, current rises only slightly while terminal voltage falls substantially, consistent with internal resistance and electrode polarization limiting performance. Common miss: Assuming an electrochemical cell always behaves as an ideal voltage source under all loads. This matches the observed current plateau and drop in terminal voltage. Source: OpenMCAT (AGPL-3.0). Unverified AI practice; not AAMC.

distractorRationales.B: Ohm's law predicts higher current for lower resistance when voltage is constant.

passage.title: Unacknowledged Method (1979)
passage.body: Pavel Hrdlička published “Unacknowledged Method” in 1979 after a season in museum captions. The argument is that institutions remember procedures better than people. The author grants that standards exist for a reason and that amateurs can be wrong. The turn is that fraud-control language is being stretched to cover disagreement. Examples accumulate without becoming a catalogue — a mistranslated notice, a map that omits a creek, a hiring rubric that scores “fit.” The prose is dry rather than outraged; the heat is in what is treated as obvious. A late paragraph asks what would have to be true for the current procedure to be called fair, and then shows that those conditions are not met. The essay does not offer a slogan. It offers a test: if a practice cannot survive being described without its official adjectives, the adjectives were doing the work. Readers who want a policy list will be disappointed; readers who want to see how a tone becomes a rule will not.

items.stem: A city fines an unlicensed drumming circle in a courtyard at 11 p.m. at the same measured level it permits from a ticketed waterfront concert with a corporate sponsor the same night. Applying the author's principle, which evaluation follows?

choices.text: The differential is automatically justified, because a ticketed event is by definition not noise.
The differential may be defensible, but only as a named political allocation of the scarce good of loudness, not as a mere meter reading.
Both events must be banned, because the author forbids all exemptions, including hospitals.
The courtyard drumming is dirt in the medical sense, so hygiene language is the only honest description.

items.explanation: The author's principle is that like sounds require like reasons and that exemptions should be named as political choices rather than as nature. A concert and a drumming circle at similar intensity, sorted by license and sponsorship, is the hymn-versus-brand structure applied to a new pair. The text allows that some exemptions (a hospital generator, perhaps a funeral) can be defended; it does not treat tickets as a natural solvent of noise, demand a total ban, or accept dirt-language as honest by default. Applying the principle therefore yields a demand for named reasons, which is B.

distractorRationales.A: Treating a ticket as a definitional escape from noise is the vitality-as-atmosphere move the walk-after-dark paragraph criticizes.
distractorRationales.C: The closing paragraph explicitly allows that a hospital generator may deserve its exemption; unlimited prohibition is refused in the fourth paragraph as well.
distractorRationales.D: Hygiene-as-dirt is the costume that lets preference skip justification; applying it here would repeat the trick, not follow the principle.

passage.title: Who may be loud
passage.body:
Noise ordinances are written as if they were thermometers. A number of decibels is named; a clock hour is named; a fine is attached. The language of public health does real work here: sleep is not a luxury, and a child whose window faces a compressor is not being precious. But the thermometer conceals a second instrument, which is a social sorting device. Cities do not merely suppress loudness. They decide which kinds of loudness will be classified as vitality and which as nuisance, and the decision tracks, with embarrassing regularity, the prestige of the people making the sound.

Walk a mixed street after dark and the taxonomy is audible. A licensed terrace with heaters and a playlist is "activation of the night-time economy." A storefront church whose singing lasts past the same hour is a complaint waiting to be logged. A terrace is a business; a congregation is a disturbance that happens to own a building. Street vendors packing ice and calling prices are "chaos"; a restaurant's Friday overflow onto the pavement is "vibrancy," provided the overflow has paid for a permit. The ear that writes the ordinance has already been trained to hear money as atmosphere and unpaid sound as aggression.

Defenders of the ordinances will say that the issue is volume, not culture. Sometimes it is. A speaker stack aimed at a bedroom is a harm whether the music is sacred or commercial. The author's claim is narrower and more awkward: when two sounds of similar intensity are sorted differently, the sorting is not acoustics. It is a theory of who belongs in the air. "Quiet" is then sold as a natural baseline, like clean water, when it is often an aesthetic associated with certain housing and certain hours of salaried rest. Night-shift workers returning at dawn, whose rest is real, rarely get to define the city's sonic morals. People who sleep when the ordinance writers sleep do.

None of this is a brief for unlimited noise, or for the romance of the unregulated street. A city that cannot protect sleep will punish the poorest first, because they cannot buy distance from compressors. The decent aim is not a louder city but a less hypocritical one: a city that admits that permission to be loud is a scarce good, distributed by licensing, policing, and taste, and that "quality of life" is never only a medical phrase. It is also a claim about whose life is the measure.

The rhetorical trick is hygiene. Once noise is framed as dirt, opposition to a particular sound can wear the costume of sanitation rather than of preference. Dirt, unlike preference, does not have to justify itself at a public meeting. It only has to be pointed at. That is why a campaign against a night market can speak the idiom of rats and refuse even when the photographs show swept stones, and why a campaign for a waterfront festival can speak the idiom of civic joy even when the sound spill is identical. The same wave-form, two moral uniforms.

If the argument holds, then reform is not a new app for logging complaints. It is a requirement that like sounds be given like reasons, and that exemptions be named as political choices rather than as nature. A hospital generator may deserve its exemption. So, perhaps, does a funeral that spills into a street. What cannot be defended is the pretense that the ordinance is only a meter reading. Meters do not know the difference between a hymn and a brand. Officials do, and they should have to say so.
